title: The Closed Doors of Dawn
story: The mist was just beginning to unravel when James reached the wide plaza of the Grand Library. He stood at the base of the massive stone steps, looking up at the colossal structure. He had never seen stone stacked so high. He had never seen doors so wide. He had never seen a dome that seemed to hold up the morning sky itself. The brass canister, secure against his chest by Barnaby's leather strap, felt like a comforting weight as he took his first steps upward. Reaching the top of the landing, James approached the grand entrance, but the massive wooden doors were firmly shut. He gave a soft pull on the heavy iron ring, but it did not budge. The library was asleep. A pale pink light began to paint the edges of Oakhaven's rooftops, signaling the very beginning of the day. James sat down on the cold stone step, wrapping his tail around his feet, and decided to wait. He watched the town slowly wake up, listening to the distant chirping of birds and the first faint hum of a far-off motor-carriage. As the sun rose higher, casting long golden shadows across the plaza, James's attention began to drift. A bright flash of light caught his eye from the street below. At the edge of the plaza, a narrow canal wound its way between the stone buildings, its water shimmering like a ribbon of liquid gold in the fresh morning light. The quiet lull of the rippling water called to him, far more enticing than the silent, locked doors. Standing up, he took one last look at the grand dome, then leaped lightly down the steps, drawn toward the sparkling path of the canal. He followed the winding towpath, watching a single autumn leaf drift slowly beneath a small stone bridge.
